newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan president says wants to meet Dalai Lama.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan president says wants to meet Dalai Lama.

text.p: Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui has asked his office to arrange a meeting with exiled Tibetan spiritual leader the Dalai Lama, Lee's spokesman said on Wednesday.

"President Lee has expressed his interest to meet with the Dalai Lama but we have not determined the time, place or nature of the meeting," spokesman Stephen Chen told Reuters. "We are currently trying to arrange such a meeting."
Such a meeting almost certainly would anger the rival communist government in China, which has warned Taiwan not to fan separatist sentiment during the Tibetan leader's visit.
The Dalai Lama, regarded by Tibetan Buddhists as a god-king but by Beijing as a "splittist" seeking Tibet's independence from communist China, plans to visit Taiwan from March 22.
Similarly, Beijing regularly condemns Lee as giving tacit support for Taiwan's formal independence from China while paying lip service to eventual reunification.
Until Wednesday, Lee's office had denied any plans to meet the Dalai Lama, who has lived in exile in India since an abortive uprising against Chinese rule in 1959.
